item.description: As floods become more frequent, severe and widespread, getting people to respond appropriately to flood warnings is more important than ever. item.description: YouGov survey finds support for tree planting and emissions taxes but opposition to air travel and fuel levies Europe live – latest updates Europeans believe human-made climate change is real, a survey has shown, with most feeling action must be taken soon – as long as they do not have to sacrifice too much to achieve it. item.description: Although global warming is set to exceed 1.5°C, financing to help communities adapt to climate change falls far short of needs, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) said in a report published on Wednesday. Fuente: UN News.

item.title: El mundo no está preparado para la adaptación climática: la financiación se queda muy corta
item.description: Los países en desarrollo necesitarán unos 305.000 millones de dólares anuales para 2035 para adaptarse al cambio climático, pero la financiación pública internacional solo alcanzó entre 28.200 y 31.700 millones en 2024 y, aunque se triplique, cubrirá como máximo el 29 % de las necesidades. Fuente: Noticias ONU.

item.title: COP31 explained: What’s at stake at this year’s UN climate summit?
item.description: The world has more tools than ever to tackle climate change, yet millions remain unable to benefit from them. As clean energy technologies advance faster than ever, the challenge facing countries at COP31 is no longer just finding solutions – but making sure everyone can afford them. Fuente: UN News.

item.description: A senior Indonesian diplomat said on Wednesday that dialogue “must not stop” among Asean members, amid a diplomatic row between Jakarta and Singapore over transboundary haze. item.title: Firework noise limit should be drastically cut to protect wild animals, UK government told
item.description: Ministers urged to go further than proposed cut to 110 decibels to ease acute stress on birds and others animals Campaigners are calling on the UK government to protect the welfare of wild animals by cutting the maximum noise level of fireworks sold to the public from 120 to 90 decibels. The Center for Wild Animal Welfare (CWAW) has said lowering the limit to 90dB – which is about one-eighth of the loudness of 120dB – would help to protect millions of wild animals from acute stress by reducing the area over which a firework disturbs surrounding wildlife. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: How penguin poo is making Antarctic snow melt faster
item.description: Researchers find the birds’ guano feeds algal blooms that absorb significantly more solar energy Penguin poo is making the Antarctic snow melt faster, a study shows. As temperatures rise, penguins are waddling closer to the south pole, with potential for this previously unrecognised phenomenon to affect a wider area. Snow algae are tiny single-celled plants that make a home in some of the coldest places on Earth. When nutrients are scarce, the algae produces red pigments to protect itself from the sun and slow growth. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.description: Farmers in Gurez store their harvests underground to last the Himalayan winter. item.title: How anxiety over climate change affects college students
item.description: College undergraduates are anxious about climate change, with many feeling powerless and frustrated about Earth's future, yet resources to help students cope are in short supply, according to new interdisciplinary University of Utah research. The sentiment isn't limited to students studying the environment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Cooking is a bigger source of harmful air particles than vehicle exhausts in London and Beijing
item.description: There have been decades of regulations to make vehicles greener and improve air quality in London and Beijing, as well as a popular shift toward less polluting road transport. Now, total emissions of harmful air pollutants from vehicle exhausts are lower than those from cooking in the centers of these two megacities, a study has found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Katy Perry faces opposition from more than 360 neighbours over proposed 110-acre California youth camp
item.description: Katy Perry’s proposed Gratitude Canyon youth camp in Goleta, California, is facing opposition from more than 360 neighbours. Residents have raised concerns about wildfire risks, traffic, noise and evacuation access. The singer’s Firework Foundation is defending the project, saying it will provide underserved children with opportunities to explore arts, nature and outdoor activities. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
